hypotheses: S : Finset (Fin8 -> Real), every member lies in Submodule.E8 Real.
epsilon : NNReal, strict2*(epsilon:Real)<Real.sqrt2. Zero radius and empty S are retained.

Second theorem C is a Finset of EuclideanSpace Real(Fin8), same cover premise and C.card=S.card. No nonempty or positive-radius hypothesis is added.
conclusion: There exists f : S -> C which is injective, with actual Real Euclidean dist(toLp2(v),f(v)) <= epsilon for every v:S.
For a finite cover with C.card=S.card there exists e:S equiv C, with the same pointwise Real-distance bound. Equiv includes surjectivity, so every supplied center is used.

proof_roadmap: Apply the actual Metric.IsCover observation at each sample point to obtain a center in C with an extended-distance bound. edist_le_ofReal converts it to the Real Euclidean-distance bound, using only nonnegativity of epsilon.

Classical.choose selects one such center per sample point. If two selected centers coincide, triangle inequality gives dist(samplev,samplew)<=2epsilon, contradicting strict2epsilon<sqrt2 together with the existing actual E8 separation bound for distinct sample values. This constructs an embedding, not only a cardinal comparison.

For finite C of equal cardinality, Fintype.card_coe identifies the two subtype cardinalities; Fintype.bijective_iff_injective_and_card turns the same embedding into a bijection. Equiv.ofBijective retains its exact forward map and hence the same closeness bound.
boundaries: The strict2epsilon<sqrt2 condition is essential for the closed-ball collision obstruction; no boundary-radius claim is made.
Centers are radius-close and are not claimed to minimize distance. Arbitrary-set injection need not be surjective; finite equal-cardinality case is an equivalence.
Classical.choice proves existence of witnesses. No matching algorithm, effective nearest-center search, runtime or computational performance result is claimed.
The domain uses actual WithLp2 Euclidean distance, not the sup norm on Fin8->Real.
No density/volume ratio/global lattice asymptotic or geometric-to-arithmetic coefficient-mass bridge is supplied.
